TRANSLATED, MEASURED 27 AUGUST 2026: 298 delivered rows against 54 «Caballeros del Temple», now swept. THE LOSING FORM WAS NOT A TYPO - «los Caballeros del Temple» is the Spanish name of the historical Knights Templar, so whoever wrote those 54 was evoking them on purpose. It was decided against because `Temple Knights` renders the Ishgardian order, not the Templars, and 298 rows already said Templo.

QIQIRN, NOT GOBLIN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. 20 delivered rows, all Qiqirn - Zuzuroon, Kikiroon and the NpcYell and Balloon lines around them. IT IS NOT A VARIANT OF [[jinglyshine]]: that is the goblin word and renders «tintinbrillo» in 35 rows. A flat count over the Spanish groups the two and reads as drift; crossed against the English they are two peoples with two words. Do not merge them.

ONE ENGLISH WORD, TWO SPANISH RENDERINGS ON PURPOSE. «piedrabrillo» in 22 rows is Roundrox's word, a goblin child; «piedra reluciente» in 14 is the narrator and everyone else. The smashed compound belongs to the speaker, not to the object. Same shape as [[sparklies]]: not drift.

GOBLIN COMPOUND: 8 delivered rows against «tratofaena» 2 and «tratejos» 1, both swept 27 August 2026. Three translators on goblin content in one night coined three forms for it. A compound is vocabulary and reads the same everywhere; two speakers being different quests does not excuse it, which is the reasoning that produced the second form.
GOBLIN COMPOUND: 9 delivered rows against «rebañogob» 5, swept. A flock is «bandada»; «rebaño» is a herd.
TRANSLATED: NOT IN THE `Item` SHEET, so 7.8 does not reach it and 7.4 translates it. Azys Lla machinery. The single delivered row that kept the English was corrected 27 August 2026.

The Carteneau ceremony is a state occasion with no clergy officiating, so not «oficio», which is religious in Spanish. The three embassy quests are the same scene told three times and must use one term.

Ya es lo que hace el corpus: 879 filas. Las 7 que quedan en ingles NO son deriva — son referencias `<sheet(AirshipExploration...)>`, que son macros, y etiquetas del taller de compania libre envueltas en `<colortype>`: «Deploy airship on exploratory voyage», «Repair airship components». Interfaz, se quedan. NO BARRAS «dirigible» A «aeronave»: el ingles usa las dos palabras y son cosas distintas. Cruzadas por gameKey el 19 de agosto de 2026, 19 de las 20 filas con «dirigible» traducen un `dirigible` ingles y la restante un `blimp` — los Ixal vuelan dirigibles y las aeronaves eorzeas son airships. Un recuento en espanol, 879 contra 20, invita a unificarlas y borraria una distincion que el original hace.
Combat mechanics vocabulary, from the guildhest briefings. Standard RPG Spanish and it matches the French.
Combat target-priority mechanic only. Narrative hostility keeps its contextual translation.

SERIES PRECEDENCE, verified rather than assumed: official Square Enix Spanish says «molbol» (Final Fantasy XII The Zodiac Age, Final Fantasy VII Remake). Outranks FFXIV's own «morbol» and the French «morbole». Same shape as moogle/moguri.
UNVERIFIED coinage. A Final Fantasy V monster with no official Spanish naming reached; the Spanish guides use the English. An official rendering outranks this. See [[gil]].

LOW CONFIDENCE. Deliberately breaks the «monstruos X» pattern of the other -kin families (seedkin, wavekin) because ashkin are the undead a revenant raises, not living creatures. fr «the damned», ja 死霊.
LOW CONFIDENCE, descriptive coinage following the French compound.

TRAP FOR A BLIND SWEEP: «carcaj» is also the ordinary Spanish noun and ships as such in InstanceContentTextData#21928 and NpcYell#11340; only the capitalised proper name is this term. Members are «los arqueros del Carcaj» or «los del Carcaj».
Lewin's rank at the head of [[Gods' Quiver]]. Neither reference helps — both flatten the title to «captain». Chosen because it works in apposition before the name: «el maestro arquero Lewin».
Not «tribus bestia». The singular «beastman» is «hombre bestia», a DIFFERENT register: 蛮族 is the collective political term the Grand Companies use, «beastmen» the word a soldier spits.
Kept distinct from [[beast tribes]] deliberately: same Japanese, different English register, and ARR uses both in the same conversations.

The unsundered Ascians. English-only — fr «divine messengers», ja «heaven's envoys» — and «paragón» is a real Spanish noun (RAE: modelo, ejemplo) that keeps the capitalised title shape. EXPECT IT TO RECUR HEAVILY from Shadowbringers on; changing it later is a large sweep.
Piratas aliados de los sahagin; no son sahagin.

The ship, feminine, and it keeps whatever <italic> macros the line carries. Translated rather than kept because it appears nowhere but inside dialogue — not a duty, not a teleport destination — which is the interface test.
Ul'dah's six oligarchs. Capitalised; the ordinary Spanish «sindicato» (a trade union) is a different word in the same shape, so a sweep must respect the capital.
Follows the English literally against a French that renames them «survivalists»; the shipped NpcYell lines already say «los Corderos».

terms.note: Forma abreviada: Amajina e Hijos; the Concern: la Compañía.
The newspaper. Keeps whatever <italic> the line carries — it is a publication title and the English italicises it.
«Liga» follows the English «League» against a French and Japanese that both say «guild». Kept parallel with [[Merchants' League]] so the two ARR leagues read as one class.

Two translators reached this independently in the same batch, which is the only kind of agreement worth recording as corroboration rather than as coincidence.
Garlean intelligence. The name is Latin in every language, so it stays; only the article is Spanish.
Nombre de empresa; concordancia singular. Skyways y Skywinds remiten a la misma compañía.
LOW CONFIDENCE coinage; neither reference fixes a term. The elementals' retribution, recurring through the Gridania arc and into Heavensward. Lowercase — a phenomenon, not a proper name.
OWNER'S RULING: the singular is «gil» and THE PLURAL IS «GILES». Not «guiles», which only the Spanish Fandom wiki asserts and no official source confirms; do not reopen it on that.
The smashed compound is the point — it is the moogle register, and «Guardia Mog» flattens it into an ordinary Spanish noun phrase.
Cosmic Exploration weather event. Coined independently and identically by two translators.
Cosmic Exploration. MassivePcContentTextData-02 coined «el traje de vacío»; sweep those lines to this if they survive.

APPLIED EVEN WHERE THE ENGLISH USES A DESCRIPTION rather than the name — «the star's previous residents», «our predecessors» — because the Japanese is 先駆者 every time. OPEN: the alternative is to reserve it for where the English capitalises.

Cosmic Exploration piloted machine. FEMININE throughout: «la mecha», «las mechas», «hangar de mechas», «pilotos de mechas». BEWARE A BLIND SWEEP: «mecha» is also the ordinary word for a fuse, used that way in Balloon#1376. Sweeping «robot» has to flip determiners too («ese robot magitek» -> «esa mecha magitek»), so do it as phrase pairs.

Cosmic Exploration creature. Kept verbatim against Spanish phonotactics, which want the prothetic e-: this project keeps invented s-plus-consonant creature names as they are, per the shipped «spriggan» and «skalla».

The ancient people of Auxesia, Cosmic Exploration. Recurs across the whole feature. See [[the Voyagers]]. Both French and Japanese say pioneer rather than traveller, which is what settles it against «los Viajeros». THE 13 «viajeros» IN THE DELIVERED CORPUS ARE NOT DRIFT: checked in context 17 August 2026 and every one is the ordinary common noun — caravans of travellers, travellers on the roads, «se aconseja a los viajeros de la zona». A count alone will keep reporting them; do not sweep without reading them.
Cosmic Exploration's mission system. Follows the English «stellar» rather than the French and Japanese «cosmic».
Instalación de Cosmic Exploration. Los nombres de cosmopuertos siguen sus propias entradas.
Cosmic Exploration hardware. Coined independently and identically by three translators.

MEDIUM. Cosmic Exploration resource. The French leans on levitation; «piedra de levitación» is the alternative if the short form reads thin. Together with «piedra clave» this sets the house pattern for the -stone family: «piedra» plus a qualifier, not a coined mineral name.

Elpis, two rows in the whole game. A translator coined «manalita» from the French «manalithe», which is well formed but does not follow this corpus: the -stone family is «piedra flotante» and «piedra clave», and «maná» is already the delivered word, 27 rows. Two precedents beat one French coinage.
The English is a portmanteau (flora + hurricane) and so is the Spanish; Balloon-12's «vendaval floral» loses that and needs sweeping if its lines survive.
Cosmic Exploration weather event. Balloon-12's «fulgor auroral» is equally defensible, but one has to win and this is it.
Cosmic Exploration ration, derived from the pinned Archon -> «Arconte». Both references localise it, so English read as a gap. Reverts to English if the item name turns out to sit on an interface.
The Crystal Exarch is a nameplate NPC, so _ui_terms_comment could argue for the English; a 64-line shipped precedent outranks it. This is what «the glossary wins» means in practice.

The Ul'dah idol trio. NOT A BLIND SWEEP TARGET: DefaultTalk#601166.22 says «las cantantes» correctly, because its English reads "those singers", a common noun rather than the group. Read the English first. The French invents a different name — see _english_names_less_than_french_comment.

THE FIRMAMENT FOREMAN, AND SHE IS FEMININE: the French marks her female throughout. «¡A sus órdenes, jefa!» for "Sir, yes, sir!" keeps the military snap. OPEN: the English deliberately varies how the workers address her (miss, sir, Chief) and flattening it to «jefa» loses that; reinstating would touch about sixty lines, rows 4967-5670.
The Firmament's reconstruction workers. Follows the French, which drops the sky metaphor. «the skybuilders' board» is «el tablón de reconstrucción».

CORREGIDO el 16 de agosto de 2026. La entrada anterior decia que se quedaba en ingles y era falsa: las siglas de estadistica van en espanol, como en el resto de la saga. El corpus decia HP en 59 sitios y PV en 5, asi que fue la mayoria la que se corrigio contra el precedente y no al reves. Las 84 apariciones se leyeron una a una antes del barrido: todas eran la estadistica, ninguna parte de un nombre propio. Va en pareja con MP -> PM y TP -> PT.

IF IT IS NOT A HOTBAR NAME, the banked Spanish is «cenizaluz».
The Time of My Life GATE. English uses a song metaphor where French and Japanese say "emote set"; the English is followed. Second/Third/Fourth Verse follow the same pattern.

Follows the job-name pattern of astrologian -> astrólogo and pictomancer -> pictomante, NOT the viper exception.
Master designa aquí a un dirigente.

POLICY CALL, OPEN: the English lowercases it in all 9 occurrences, so it was treated as prose — but the duty ACTION on the hotbar is "Medical Kit", which _ui_terms_comment could claim. Reversing is 8 lines of GimmickTalk-01.

Lowercase, following the English. CASE SEAM: NpcYell-24 shipped «¡Usando Fortis!» capitalised, presumably because the English capitalises it there. «vial of salutaris» -> «un frasco de salutaris» (帝国式回復剤); the French collapses the two items into one and the English does not.
Nymeia, of the Twelve. Matches the agent-noun shape of la Matrona, el Errante, la Furia. Not «la Tejedora».

TRES SENTIDOS, NO DOS. (1) La unidad de tiempo: Eorzea cuenta las horas en bells, «campanada», 113 filas. (2) Una campana de mano, como la que llama al retainer, «campanilla», 25 filas, fijado el 13 de agosto de 2026 sobre 33 filas y con ello cerrada la duda que planteaba Balloon#2993. (3) EL CASCABEL QUE LLEVAN LOS NAMAZU AL CUELLO, «cascabel», 5 filas entregadas, una explícita: «The bells you see at our necks». El tercer sentido se añade el 15 de agosto tras marcarlo el comprobador en nam-desc-01: el traductor había seguido el corpus y era esta entrada la que estaba incompleta.

The setting's gunpowder: fr «poudre», ja 火薬. Not «arena de fuego», a literal calque. TWO STRAGGLERS STILL NEED SWEEPING, NpcYell#1242 and Balloon#2106 — and the second writes «arena
de fuego», so a search for the plain phrase misses it. Any multi-word term an authored
splits has this blind spot.
Short form of the recorded «la Santa Sede», used where the English itself shortens it to «the See». Do not expand the short form.

KEPT ENGLISH BECAUSE NO OFFICIAL SPANISH RENDERING WAS FOUND TO OUTRANK IT, not because the corpus already had one — a shipped rendering never settles a series term. The only results reachable were Fandom wikis, which the fan-source trap excludes. Reopen if an official Spanish source turns up.
The non-Elder Seedseers of Gridania, from the pinned «Gran Vidente».
Consistent with the pinned «las Llamas Inmortales». The French substitutes his surname instead of the title, which _english_names_less_than_french_comment says to ignore.

From the pinned «el Barrio Alamhigano». Capitalised as a people per _peoples_casing_comment. The English clips «Ala Mhigan» to «Mhigan»; Spanish does not clip it. ONE WORD, NOT TWO. COUNTING TRAP: a substring count of «mhigano» reports 76 lines and looks like an overwhelming lowercase convention, but 70 are the tail of «Alamhiganos» matching inside itself. Count with a word boundary.
F'lhaminn's epithet. The French invents a different epithet entirely, so _english_names_less_than_french_comment applies and the English is followed.
A children's game, named only in prose and in no sheet.
Both French and Japanese add "coral" and the English withholds it, so _english_names_less_than_french_comment applies: follow the English and do not import the qualifier.

An inn built under a lichyard. TRANSLATED ON PURPOSE against the general place rule: Balloon#1057 jokes about the name being a poor choice for an inn, and the joke dies if the name is opaque. The Earthenshire reasoning in reverse.
Chosen over «camposanto» for consistency with 3 shipped «cementerio». The English word is archaic where the Spanish is neutral, and no Spanish archaism was available that a bubble could hold.

terms.note: Nombre de empresa; concordancia femenina singular.
A goblin word for offspring. Rendered identically in both rows that use it (Balloon#1534 and #1538) to preserve the callback between them.
Goblin compound, built on the recorded brainfruit -> «frutosesos». Smashed compound with no diminutive, per _moblin_register_comment.
Goblin word for a Lalafell.
Vath term for the player. The Japanese ウデキキ is 腕利き, "skilled hand".
Goblin word for a firearm.
Goblin word for food.

Goblin compound; the gobbie- prefix is kept as gobbi-.
Goblin abstract noun for cleverness.
Goblin name, Balloon#1674. Follows the shipped smashed-compound style.
Sahagin term, Balloon#1666. Hooks the recorded salt -> «sal» and the «cruzar la sal» idiom rather than following the French, which flattens it to "mistress".
LOW CONFIDENCE. A slur for the Sahagin; the French drops the slur and uses the real name. «escamosos» was unavailable — 17 shipped lines use it for scalekin mobs generally.
An NPC's invented move rather than a hotbar ability, so _ui_terms_comment does not reach it, and the French translated it.
DELIBERATELY UNACCENTED. The moogle entry reserves «kupó» for the interjection and leaves «Kupka» and «kupoteros» unaccented; the nut follows those, not the interjection. Plural: nueces de kupo.

THE FRENCH DECIDES IT: of the five corpus lines that name them, only Balloon#2046 has a French rendering, «du piment dragon», the compound rather than a generic chilli. Not «guindillas de dragón». Balloon#3222 needs sweeping.
A child mispronouncing "culinarian". Lambdacismo, which _sugar_riot_ceceo_comment itself names as the canonical Spanish baby-talk marker.
MEDIUM-LOW, flagged by its translator. Kept as a coinage rather than normalised to «día» because the English is deliberately non-standard and the register depends on it.
Lowercase produce, translated following the French, which translates every one of this family.
Lowercase produce; see milkroot.
Lowercase produce; see milkroot.
Lowercase produce; see milkroot.
Lowercase produce; see milkroot.
A wine. Lowercase produce; see milkroot. Note Millioncorn is CAPITALISED in the English and therefore stays English — the lowercase test is what separates them.

Ruler of Tuliyollal, 282 occurrences. «servidor» is the word Spanish uses for office-holders; «sirviente» implies domestic service and is wrong for a monarch. Pairs with Landsguard and Dawnherald in a «del Alba» family. Plural: Servidores del Alba. GENDER RULE: as the NAME OF THE OFFICE it is masculine and invariable («el elector del Servidor del Alba»), but PREDICATED OF WUK LAMAT HERSELF it agrees («voy a ser Servidora del Alba»). English cannot show the difference; Spanish must.

Dawntrail lore concept, 166 occurrences. Neither French nor Japanese carries the title at all — both say princess/prince plus the name. It is an invention of the English localisation, and translated rather than dropped because English is what the player sees.
Zoraal Ja. Same reasoning as Third Promise.
Koana. Same reasoning as Third Promise.

Tuliyollal's standing army. THE GENDER CHANGES from masculine to feminine, so sites need their articles fixed by hand («del Landsguard» -> «de la Legión del Alba»); a blind find-and-replace produces wrong agreement.
One of Gulool Ja Ja's two heads, the deliberative one.
The other head, the martial one. French says 'Force' and Japanese 武 (martial); Spanish follows the English 'Resolve'.
The epic carved on the pillars, divided into the seven 'Lay of' chapters below.

Chapter of the Tuliyollal Saga. «Cantar» is the Spanish term for an epic lay (Cantar de mio Cid); French and Japanese both flatten it to «chapter». Attested: Brotherhood/Hermandad, Repast/Festín, Reeds/Juncos, Pots/Vasijas, Gold/Oro, Proof/Pruebas, Ice/Hielo.
The trials set by each elector during the rite of succession.
The seven judges of the rite of succession. Lowercase common noun; inflect for gender when the elector is known (Zanuhali is female: 'electora').
Epithet of Valigarmanda. French and Japanese both say 'living calamity'; Spanish keeps the English compound because it functions as a title.
Goldsmiths under contract to the Moblins, named for their pot-shaped workshops. Invariable in the plural. See [[_moblin_register_comment]].

Erenville's lodestone. English coins an opaque name and explains it two lines later («Pairing stones are natural magnets»); «piedra imán» would turn that reveal into a tautology, so «compañera» carries the pairing without spoiling it. English's «Alluring, isn't it?» puns on attraction, and «Atrayente, ¿verdad?» does the same.
Beach below Tuliyollal. WARNING: French and Japanese attach a proper name, «Gornitruq», that the English does not have. Do not import it. See [[_english_names_less_than_french_comment]].
The Mamool Ja memorial at the mouth of the Skydeep Cenote, where the children sacrificed to conceive blessed siblings are laid. Common noun, lowercase.
Femenino «astróloga». Ver `_job_names_stay_english_comment`.

FFXIV job name. In KinGmc104 English says «you are an accomplished culinarian» about the player, which is neutral in English and not in Spanish — wrap it: «<if(gnum4,una cocinera consumada,un cocinero consumado)>».

Xbr'aal village east of Iq Br'aax, destroyed in the war with the Mamool Ja. Proper name, untouched. English calls it «the village of» where Japanese says «the houses of»; Spanish follows English with «poblado», the established word for tribal settlements.

Mamool Ja slur-prefix for outsiders, built on «across the salt». Attested: «un demonio salado en carne y hueso». It reads odd in Spanish and it reads odd in English too — that is the point. When it modifies a noun that agrees, wrap the whole phrase: «tu <if(gnum4,amiga salada,amigo salado)>». See [[salt-licker]].

Spice that colours xibruq pibil. Left as-is because it is ALREADY the Spanish word (the bixa/annatto seed). English quotes it as an exotic loanword and the quotes are kept, because Krile presents it as a term she has just learned. French substitutes «roucou».

KEPT ENGLISH per the creature ruling: a sprite is not a Final Fantasy icon the glossary pins. A PIN THAT COVERS ONE MEMBER OF A FAMILY SPLITS IT, and nothing detects that — this entry once said «espíritu de fuego» and left it standing beside `earth sprite` and the rest in English. All seven elements are English now. If the deferral is ever lifted, lift it for the family at once: espíritu de fuego / tierra / viento / agua / rayo / hielo / tormenta.

Insult a Mamool Ja lackey throws at the Warrior of Light in KinGmc102. Hooks into the established «across the salt» -> «allende la sal» for foreigner, which is how the English insult works. Neither French nor Japanese has it.

terms.ja: エーテルを検知する魔法人形
terms.note: Erenville's gleaner tool, a floating magicked hand. «Rastreador» and not «buscador» because every line talks about following a trail, not locating a point. IN KinGmb113_04892 English italicises «handy» because the device IS a hand and Wuk Lamat pays it off; the Spanish keeps the joke with «echar una <italic(1)>mano<italic(0)>». See [[gleaner]].

THE PLANET ONLY. Balloon#2986 is an astronomer on a literal star in the sky and is correctly «la estrella». FFXIV's own word for the planet, where plain «world» would do; French flattens it to «ce monde» and «astro» keeps the deliberate strangeness.

What the Meso Terminal becomes once Sphene's living memories are wiped. THE ENGLISH ALSO WRITES IT INVERTED — «Queen Eternal» at InstanceContentTextData#42106, same referent, ja エターナルクイーン either way. Both render «la Reina Eterna». Recorded because the drift checker matches on the English string and is blind to the inverted variant.
Alexandria's combat machine, whose battle data the Eternal Queen cites when singling out the Warrior of Light. Translated in every language.
The Warrior of Light's gift, and Krile's. Series-wide term. Japanese describes it functionally; English and French name it, and so does Spanish. Distinct from «Worlar's Echo», which is a place.
Krile's birth name, given by Robor and Alayla. Her full name is Krile Maya Baldesion. Untranslated.
Standing FFXIV discipline. Rendered descriptively as French does rather than kept as the coined English noun, since Spanish has no established form.
Alexandria's founding festival, replayed endlessly in Living Memory. Translated in every language.

The expansion's central MacGuffin, shipped across the KinGma quests. Japanese 黄金郷 is the standard word for El Dorado; Spanish deliberately does NOT use «El Dorado», which would import a real-world legend the text never invokes. Not «ciudad de oro».
Standing FFXIV term. Already shipped in VoiceMan_07003 ('Los ascianos sin duda lo llamarían una Reunificación').

The post-duty vote. THE VERB IS «recomendar» and «Player Commendation» is «Recomendación de jugador». Owner's decision. HOMONYM TRAP, AND IT IS ENORMOUS: «encomendar» is ordinary Spanish for entrusting a task — «ha encomendado» appears 64 times, «te encomienda» 24, none of it this mechanic. NEVER SWEEP «encomienda» OR «encomendar». «encomiable» at InstanceContentTextData#35216 is the adjective and stays; 54 lines rendering an ordinary «commend» as «elogiar»/«felicitar» are praise, not the mechanic, and stay too. HowToPage#1521 keeps the button in English on purpose: it points at an `Addon` label the game still draws in English.

And the verb `desynthesize` is «desintetizar». Owner's decision, against «descomponer/descomposición». English coined the word as the reverse of SYNTHESIS, which is what this game calls crafting, and the corpus ships «síntesis» 117 times and «sintetizar» 55; the internal pairing outranks the Japanese 分解 and the French «recyclage». HOMONYM TRAP: NEVER SWEEP THE BARE WORD. Six lines use «descomposición» in its ordinary sense (rotting carrion, a corpse, decomposing memories), and aetherial reduction is a different mechanic whose «descompone» also stays. Every rule that made this change was a phrase, never a word. A THIRD RENDERING, «desintegrar/desintegración», survived the first sweep and needed its own — counting only the losing form you already know about is how that happens. Its homonym is one line away: GimmickTalk#43's «desintegración de la personalidad» stays.
Standing FFXIV term. Pairs with 'the void' -> el Vacío and 'voidsent' -> seres del Vacío.
The thirteenth reflection, the void's own shard. Pairs with 'reflection' -> reflejo.

Wuk Lamat's title after taking the throne. Matches «King of Resolve» -> Rey de la Resolución and «Vow of Reason» -> Juramento de la Razón. French collapses Vow and Promise into «Aurarque» and loses the distinction Spanish keeps.
Standing FFXIV term, brought in by Y'shtola when she compares soul harvesting to voidsent practice. Pairs with 'the void' -> el Vacío.
Llymlaen. Eorzean oath, so it appears in the mouths of Eorzean characters (Ketenramm) even in Turali scenes. Kept as the deity rather than flattened to a generic '¿qué demonios...?'.

Zoraal Ja's soulless machine soldiers. English is reaching for Eliot on purpose and French drops the image entirely; «hombres huecos» is the standard rendering of the poem's title and lands the same way.
Zoraal Ja's order to execute Alexandria's civilians and harvest their souls. Kept as a flat military codename — the horror is that it is filed like any other operation.
Almas preservadas de Alexandria. No aplicar al adjetivo común endless ni a topónimos que lo contengan.

The machine that dispenses souls for credits. Part of the consumer vocabulary Alexandria uses to normalise its soul trade — credits -> créditos, spare souls -> almas de repuesto, regulators -> reguladores. Keep all of it flat and administrative: the scene works because Sphene explains it like a vending machine. «spare souls» is NOT merged with [[soul cell]] — two different English formulations.

Where Alexandrians say forgotten people have gone. English is doing two things at once — a homely euphemism for the dead AND literal data storage — and «la nube» means exactly those two things today. French flattens it to «les cieux» and keeps only the euphemism, losing the technological chill. Do not follow French.
Alexandria's stored souls. English deliberately phrases them like a consumable product; keep the flat, clinical register — the horror comes from how ordinary the characters make it sound.
The Ascians' world-merging. 'Ascians' -> ascianos.
Alexandria's power source. Coined substance name, kept as-is like [ceruleum].

Erenville's birth name, used only by his mother Cahciua. Untouched. Her pet name for him, «fussy little bunbun», renders as «conejito quisquilloso» and is quoted back in a dialogue option, so the two must match.
Queen of Reason of Alexandria. Proper name, untouched.

Alexandria mirrors Tuliyollal's two-ruler system, but English uses Queen/King here where Tuliyollal uses [[Vow]]. So NOT «Juramento» — and «King of Resolve» likewise renders «Rey de la Resolución». Japanese uses the same 理王/武王 for both realms; English draws the distinction and English is the reference.
The bomb train. Joins the 'del Alba' family, reads like a real locomotive name, and keeps the double sense of 'blaze' (to trail-blaze / to burn) — which is literally what the train does.

The Eorzean order. «Amanecer» NOT «Alba», deliberately: «Alba» is reserved for the Tural family of titles ([[Dawnservant]], [[Landsguard]], the Dawnherald), and reusing the word would silently imply a connection the story never makes.
Established Final Fantasy XIV term for the shards of the Source. Lowercase.
Capitalised as a place. 'voidgate' -> 'puerta del Vacío'.

terms.ja: バルデシオンアーセナル
terms.note: TRANSLATED, AND IT IS AN INSTANCE — the exception that shows what the interface-vs-prose test actually tests. A duty name normally stays English because the player reads it in the Duty Finder, and this one IS a 56-player raid; but it is NOT IN THE FINDER at all. It is entered from inside Eureka Hydatos, so a player never meets the string as an interface entry, and the Duty Finder list does not carry it. The test is where the name is READ, not what kind of thing it names. Decided 17 August 2026 when the svc-03 translator followed the glossary against its own keep-English instinct and asked for the reconciliation; it was right. The one holdout, PublicContentTextData#2132 «Conquista el Baldesion Arsenal», was swept at the same time.
Shaaloani outlaw gang that Wihuwte took over. French drops the name and just says 'gang'. 'Albores' is a real Spanish word for daybreak and reads like a gang name; short enough for the length budget.
Wihuwte's outlaw alias. Translated in every language.

Title of the CROWNED rulers — «Vow Koana», «the Vow of Resolve». English deliberately opposes it to [[Promise]], the title held while still a claimant, so the pair must survive: Promise -> Promesa, Vow -> Juramento. That is the escalation from a pledge made to a pledge that binds. French collapses both into «Aurarque»; do not follow it. Accepted cost: «Juramento» is masculine and also applies to Wuk Lamat, which works the way «Su Alteza» does for a man.
Shaaloani's peacekeeping force. French flattens it to 'milice' and drops the coined name; English keeps it and so do we. 'deputy chief' -> 'subjefe'.
Erenville's home region. Untouched.
Established Final Fantasy XIV substance. Untouched.
Tipo de cactilio. Mantener sabotender como denominación específica; cactuar se traduce cactilio.
Plural: cactilios. Se mantiene la distinción con sabotender; los nombres de objetos y destinos protegidos siguen en inglés.

Generic term for Tural's border gates. Only one instance appears so far and it is always the Xak Tural one — see [[Xak Tural Skygate]], whose established rendering wins whenever the destination is named.
Winner of the Hanuhanu wind-magic contest.
The Ihih'hana procession. French refers to it only as 'la procession d'Ihih'hana'.

Creature class, lowercase in English and kept verbatim by every localisation. WARNING — INVARIABLE, INCLUDING IN THE PLURAL: «los tural vidraal», never «los vidraal turales». «Tural» reads like a postposed Spanish adjective and is not one. Eight lines across KinGmb110, KinGmb111 and KinGmb113 had drifted before this was caught. The drift checker cannot see it: it only inspects protect:false terms.
Hanuhanu harvest festival.
Established series term; French adapts it, Spanish-speaking players use the English form.
Wuk Lamat's lineage — 'Wuk Lamat of the Dawn's Promise'. Neither French nor Japanese carries it; consistent with the Promise titles and the 'del Alba' family.
What Bakool Ja Ja calls himself: a two-headed Mamool Ja born of a Hoobigo and a Boonewa. Plural because the two heads are two brothers — keep the plural in Spanish even though one body speaks.

SPEAKER FIELD, not dialogue — the war head. Register: arrogant, mocking, calls Wuk Lamat a house cat. The other head is «Bakool Ja Ja the Mystic» (魔), the eager younger brother. They address each other as «Brother»; keep the two voices distinct.

Krile's scholarly order. «Estudiantes» would read as a school class; «Discípulos» carries membership in an order, which is what French «Élèves» and Japanese 委員会 both point at. Singular for a member: «Discípula de Baldesion».

The pre-Tuliyollal Mamool Ja kingship, chosen by the original rite of succession — only the two-headed were eligible. French and Japanese flatten it to plain «king»; English keeps the distinct title and so does Spanish, because the point of the line is that Gulool Ja Ja borrowed an older institution.
Mamool Ja mercenary warband, returned broken from overseas and now chasing the golden city.
Gulool Ja Ja's pet name for Wuk Lamat. Family only.

Epithet of Zoraal Ja. Japanese says «miracle child» and French «Enfant prodige»; English alone says «Resilient», pointing at enduring rather than at wonder. Already shipped in KinGma113_04872 — do not re-decide it. No article in the term itself: «inspirados en el Hijo Resiliente».

terms.es-es: en la columna de los millares
terms.note: PELUPELU SPEECH, NOT A NUMBER FORMAT. They say «ten pel... in the thousands column» for 10,000. French and Japanese both flatten it to the plain figure — do NOT follow them: the joke is that Wuk Lamat converts it in her head, gets it wrong, and Erenville corrects her. Flattening makes two lines meaningless. Companion: «in the hundreds column» -> «en la columna de las centenas».
Tobli's title. English puns on ledger = accounts + leader; Spanish keeps the merchant flavour. His other title, 'head rancher', is 'capataz del rancho'.
The seven stones fitted into the claimants' tablets.
Scented saddle used to calm a wild alpaca.

terms.ja: 計り知れぬほど価値ある品
terms.note: The dungeon's MacGuffin phrase. Recurs across 43675, 43694, 43762, 43764 and is italicised in French, so it has to read identically each time or the running joke — nobody can agree what it is — stops landing.

The Corvosian sword-and-aether tradition wiped out by the Empire. Lowercase common noun; the one met in the dungeon is female, so «maestra de la espada». Not «espadachín»: ja 剛剣使い and fr «maître d'armes» both stress mastery of a school, not mere swordsmanship.

terms.es-es: la Maestra de la Espada Solitaria
terms.note: Boss name as it appears in the duty objective. Feminine — the party dialogue refers to her as «she». French drops «Lone» entirely; English keeps it and English is the reference.

The swordmaster's art, named as a thing to be witnessed. Japanese 剛剣 is the same word behind [[swordmaster]] (剛剣使い = wielder of the 剛剣); French collapses both into «maître d'armes» and cannot distinguish the art from its practitioner. Spanish keeps them separate, as English does.

First boss: an indolent fire spirit who orders her carpets to fight for her. «Pari» is the Persian peri and stays; the epithet is translated, as French does not carry it at all and leaving it English would read as a gap in the objective.
Second boss. Name untouched, epithet translated («sea-maid» = 人魚, plain mermaid). Her register is lyrical and uses plural «vosotros» for the party, following the French «vous».
Landmark: two rock formations flanking a strait, said to be the ankles of a colossal statue. Translated in every language; 'Corvos' (the Ilsabard region) is untouched.
Y'nazqha's trade — she describes herself as having a «gleaner's intuition» («instinct de glaneuse»). Feminine «espigadora» for her. «Recolector» would flatten it into generic gathering.

FEMININE in Spanish — watch agreement («mandó levantar una»). This note existed and 45 lines drifted masculine anyway, because §2 of the spec offered «Te has sintonizado con el eterita» as its own example of system register. The example is fixed; if it ever comes back, so does the drift.

Título sharlayano. Es un rango formal, no una descripción, así que «Arconte» y no «sabio», que queda libre para el sage llano. Plural: Arcontes. «Operation Archon» pasa a «Operación Arconte». EXCEPCIÓN: «Archon egg», con o sin adjetivo delante, SE QUEDA EN INGLÉS por la regla de los nombres de objeto. El validador la marca cada vez porque casa la palabra suelta dentro del nombre; no es deriva.

terms.ja: マーチ・オブ・アルコンズ
terms.note: The joint Alliance operation. French renames it entirely; Japanese transliterates the English.
Seasonal military exercise during the Rising.
Critical Encounter title from DynamicEvent. Keep it in English while that sheet is outside the pack.
Plural: encargados de objetos perdidos.
'the Calamity' -> 'la Calamidad'. Capitalised as an event name.
Companion forms: 'Seventh Umbral Era' -> 'Séptima Era Umbral'.
Same pattern for the other eras: 'Seventh Astral Era' -> 'Séptima Era Astral'.
Louisoix's secret order. Follows the French, which is the closest of the three to the English.
Ul'dah's Grand Company. Feminine plural in Spanish — 'las Llamas Inmortales'.
Gran Compañía de Gridania. Usar «la Orden de las Víboras Gemelas».
Plural 'Grandes Compañías'. The Maelstrom keeps its English name ('el Maelstrom').

terms.ja: エオルゼア都市軍事同盟
terms.note: Feminine. Preferred over 'Alianza Eorzeana' because Spanish has no settled adjective for Eorzea.
The Immortal Flames' adventurer unit. French and Japanese both describe it rather than name it.
The Empire's plan to bring Dalamud down. Lowercase 'proyecto', as in the English and French.
Also appears as 'transmission tower' -> 'torre de transmisión'; both name the same device.

Lowercase common noun, inflects: 'la primigenia Garuda', 'los primigenios'. 'elder primal' -> 'primigenio ancestral'. 1,236 shipped rows and NO competing rendering. DO NOT RE-REPORT «primordial» AS DRIFT: 26 rows carry it and every one is the ordinary Spanish adjective — «la seguridad de los rehenes es lo primordial», «el objetivo primordial», «el equilibrio primordial» — never the creature. Reported as a conflict by the sb-cs-02 translator on 15 August; checked and dismissed.
Pins the 'es' the generated glossary has no field for. Inflects for the player: '<if(gnum4,Guerrera,Guerrero)> de la Luz'.
How NPCs address the player. Inflects: '<if(gnum4,heroína,héroe)> de Eorzea'.
Kan-E-Senna's office. French and Japanese both substitute her name; Spanish keeps the title so the English reference survives.
The artefact used to open the way into Garuda's domain.
Ifrit's epithet. French and Japanese drop it and use the name.
Nael van Darnus's epithet. French says 'silver raptor'; Spanish follows the English.
Garlean legion commander. Lowercase before a name ('el legado Nael van Darnus'), matching Spanish usage for Roman ranks.
The Eorzean pantheon.
'Battle of Carteneau' -> 'batalla de Carteneau'.

Gurfurlur's title among the Yok Huy: a priest-seer, not a chieftain. French flattens it to «grand chaman» and loses the light imagery, which matters because the whole expansion runs on dawn/light vocabulary. «Lumbrera» is a real Spanish word for an eminent figure and keeps that root. Plural «luminaries» -> «lumbreras».
Giant race of Kozama'uka. CAPITALISED always, including adjectivally: «los Yok Huy», «la antigua lengua Yok Huy». Normal Spanish would lowercase an ethnonym; see _peoples_casing_comment.
Cattle-like beast herded by the nomadic Turali Miqo|te. Creature name, untouched.
Riverboat-hauling beast. Creature name, untouched.
Merchant race. English says 'Pelu', French 'pelupelu' — follow English. Lowercase adjectivally: 'un mercader pelu'.
Mamool Ja clan name. Untouched.
Yok Huy elector. Proper name, untouched.
Jefe guerrero Yok Huy de las salinas de Chirwagur. Nombre propio.

terms.en: Ignorance begets strife. Understanding begets fellowship.
terms.fr: De l'ignorance naît le conflit... De la tolérance fleurira l'harmonie.
terms.ja: 無知ゆえに争い、知りて絆を結ぶ
terms.es-es: De la ignorancia, discordia. Del entendimiento, concordia.
terms.note: Gulool Ja Ja's maxim and the thematic spine of the expansion; recurs verbatim and in fragments, so it is pinned. Rendered as an elliptical aphorism rather than word for word — the literal version overshot the length threshold and read like a school motto. discordia/concordia is the natural Spanish antonym pair and lands as a proverb, which is what the English parallelism achieves. The two halves are spoken by the two heads in turn, which suits the ellipsis. «Hermandad» is deliberately NOT used here — it is reserved for [[Brotherhood]].

Feeds the Lay of / Feat of pattern: «Cantar de la Hermandad», «Prueba de la Hermandad». French and Japanese say «friendship»; English says Brotherhood and English is the reference. Kept distinct from «fellowship» in Gulool Ja Ja's maxim, which is «concordia».
Autarch of Mamook, elector for the Feat of the Brotherhood, and Bakool Ja Ja's father. Proper name, untouched.
Banana variety whose leaf is the essential xibruq pibil wrapping — the ingredient Sareel Ja fails to obtain. Proper name, untouched.
Beast whose meat goes into xibruq pibil. Creature name, untouched.

Xbr'aal foodstuff, steamed. Untouched. THE ENGLISH IS INCONSISTENT: 07002 001370 says «najool leaf» where 001270 says «Ja Tiika banana leaf» and the Japanese uses the same term in both. Each line follows its own English.

The ocean, in Turali idiom — «cross the salt». Also a vocative slur for outsiders («Don't look away, salt!»), kept as «sal» there too: it is opaque, deliberately alien slang in English as well, and it hooks back to «cruzar la sal».

Mamool Ja born with two heads; «one-head» is its insult-counterpart («de una cabeza»). Deliberately NOT «bicéfalo»/«monocéfalo»: the English is blunt schoolyard vocabulary used as a taunt, where the -céfalo pair reads like a medical textbook — and the clinical forms are what French reaches for, so they look right and are wrong. Cost accepted: the periphrasis is longer, so short taunts need rewording rather than literal translation.
Hunter tribe of Yak T'el. Proper name, untouched. Lowercase when adjectival ('cazadores xbr'aal'), capitalised as a noun ('los Xbr'aal').
Xbr'aal chieftain title. English keeps the native term untranslated; French flattens it to 'chef du village' and Japanese to 族長. Following English and keeping it.
Water-filled sinkhole. No coining needed: Spanish already has this exact word, borrowed from Yucatec Maya, and it means precisely what Erenville describes.
Traditional Xbr'aal dish, untouched in every language. Echoes the real-world cochinita pibil, so it reads as food to a Spanish player without any help.
Feeds the Lay of / Feat of pattern: 'Cantar del Festín', 'Prueba del Festín'.

Gurfurlur's feat, held among the living sepulchres. French and Japanese name it after the SETTING («trial of the tombs»); English names what is being demonstrated, and «testimonio» is apt because the monuments bear witness to the deeds inscribed on them. PROVISIONAL.
The feat that was to reinforce Valigarmanda's seal, cancelled once Bakool Ja Ja broke it. Same split as [[Feat of Proof]]: French and Japanese say «seal», English says «ice». PROVISIONAL.

A monument raised while the honouree is still ALIVE. NOT a grave: Gulool Ja Ja is alive and has one, and Wuk Lamat mistakes it for a grave precisely because of that. If the distinction collapses in Spanish, the scene stops making sense.
The tural vidraal sealed in ice beneath Worqor Zormor. Proper name, untouched. Referred to as the Skyruin — see that entry.
Yok Huy luminary serving under Gurfurlur. Proper name, untouched.
Limsa Lominsa explorer, first outsider to reach Tural; named on Gulool Ja Ja's living sepulchre. Proper name. 'Lominsan' renders as 'de Limsa Lominsa' — there is no settled Spanish demonym.
Madre de Erenville, del pueblo Shetona. Concordancia femenina.
Proper name, untouched.
The recurring Final Fantasy creature, not an explosive device. Translated in every language and rendered «Bomba» by the Spanish Final Fantasy titles, so English would read as a gap. Plural: bombas.
Keep Oblivion for the Alexandrian resistance. The Snowcloak arena is Olvido (French: Cirque aux stalactites; Japanese: 氷柱の円庭).
Patch 7.5 lore term. FR and JA both say "the end of tomorrows"; English coins "Solstice" and English is the reference. Pairs with Invernantes.
Calyx faction. "Invernante" is a real Spanish word for one who winters somewhere, reads as a coined faction name, and keeps the winter root tying it to Solsticio.
True name of the key. Spanish already has the word; kept capitalised as a name.
Pairs with "escindido" already used for the Sundering. FR and JA say "the originals"; English is the reference.
Containment crystal. MASCULINE deliberately: FR made it masculine to keep it off "mémoire", and Spanish must too, or "la memoria de Enuo" reads as "Enuo's memory".
Mare Lamentorum sealing mechanism. "Brand" here is the archaic word for sword; FR and JA both say sword, and the structures are sword-shaped.
Accent required by Spanish stress rules; matches FR.
Generated glossary says protect:false because FR renames it. Following FR would produce a form no Spanish player recognises; the Spanish Final Fantasy releases use Zodiark.
FR uses its own digraph; English form kept.
FR adapts, so Spanish adapts in parallel. Feminine for individuals: "la mejor Loporrita". PROVISIONAL — revisit if Endwalker throws up a better form.
Already shipped in VoiceMan_07004 and 07200 but never recorded. Pinned.
Translated in every language. Not the housing district — see the Oblivion note on homonym collisions.
Fisura entre planos. No confundir con La Fisura, el espacio entre dimensiones.
Follows English "actuation" rather than FR "control".
Job name. Same treatment as astrologian -> astrólogo, culinarian -> cocinero.
Series-wide term with an established Spanish rendering. Distinct from "the aetherial sea" -> el mar etéreo, which FR conflates with it.
Follows English "contingent" over FR "délégation".

Unified on the cutscene form, the canonical MSQ text, against «el Embate de las Tormentas» in three KinGmi/j quests. Recorded so the drift check can catch a recurrence; it could not before, because it only sees terms written down.
Three translators proposed this independently, which is why it is here rather than under debate. Invariable in the plural, «los devorapecados», like «cortafuegos».

Mind-bound to a primal. Two translators split between «subyugado» and «sometido»; subyugado follows the French and is the stronger word, which the concept needs. One shipped line was changed to match.
Bare «the Warden» in the same scenes is «el Guardián».
An adjective, so it inflects: allagana, allaganos.
Goblin-speak. Follows the smashed-compound pattern of braincase -> cascosesos, with no diminutive. «altoterrano» was the rival coinage; the cruder compound is the more goblin.
Goblin-speak. See uplander; 15 lines unified.
Goblin-speak. See uplander; 12 lines unified off «chisporrotines», whose diminutive breaks the pattern.
Halone's epithet. The generated glossary carries only «Halone», and the French «la Conquérante» does not read as an epithet in a shout.
Brass is latón. The French says copper and is simply wrong; this is one of the places the reference cannot be followed.

OWNER'S RULING: the English stays. Same reasoning as the Duty Finder and the Gold Saucer — the `Addon` rows that label the FC window are untranslated, so an NPC saying «tu compañía libre» points the player at a button that reads Free Company, and the community says FC in any case. 193 lines had shipped as «compañía libre» against 24 that kept the English and were swept. AGREEMENT IS UNCHANGED: it stays feminine singular, so «la/una/tu/ninguna Free Company» all still work, and the plural is «Free Companies». `Grand Company` is NOT covered — it is «Gran Compañía» in 320 shipped lines with none in English, and reversing that is the owner's call.

KEPT ENGLISH, confirmed rather than assumed: the official Spanish release of Final Fantasy VIII left the card game untranslated. That is the deciding evidence under the series-precedent rule, and it agrees with _ui_terms_comment, since the player opens a Triple Triad window. 46 translated occurrences of «Triple Tríada» STILL NEED SWEEPING, and no check will find them: protect:true skips the drift checker, and «Triple Tríada» is a DIFFERENT SPANISH rather than leftover English, which is the only thing that checker looks for. Any sweep has to come from a direct search.
Plural: encargos de gremio. La forma abreviada leve se traduce como encargo cuando designa esta tarea.
38 occurrences shipped. No English occurrences.

terms.es-es: la Vigilia de Todos los Santos
terms.note: THE VALUE WAS FIRST WRITTEN AS «Todos los Santos», WHICH WAS A DEFECT: it is a substring of the form actually shipped, so the drift check passed whichever of the two a translator wrote and the entry constrained nothing. A GLOSSARY VALUE HAS TO BE THE WHOLE PHRASE OR IT IS DECORATION.
13 shipped against 6 English. Sweep the 6.
8 shipped against 1 English. Sweep the 1.

THE ENGLISH CLIPS IT TO A BARE «Starlight» far more often than it writes the full name — «what would you like for Starlight this year?» — and this key does not match that, so a translator who looks it up finds nothing and coins one. SPANISH DOES NOT CLIP: write «la Fiesta de las Estrellas» wherever the English says Starlight on its own. Same shape as the Ala Mhigan clip and the Hatching-tide key. Sweep any «Celebración Estelar» or «la Luz Estelar».
25 shipped against 15 English — the closest of the eight. Sweep the 15.

THE KEY CARRIES A HYPHEN AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. 164 apariciones de «engarce»/«engarzar» en el corpus contra 3 de «acoplar», asi que no era una eleccion sino deriva; barridas el 16 de agosto de 2026. ES ADEMAS LA PALABRA EXACTA: engarzar es montar una piedra en un metal, que es lo que hace la materia en una ranura, y el frances dice «sertir», que es lo mismo. «Acoplar» es de mecanica -- el corpus lo usa bien en «acoplar piezas a los drones» -- y aplicado a una gema magica chirria. Una fila lo llevaba dentro de la misma frase: ClsGld200_00615 decia «acoplar estos cristales» y «quiero que engarce una materia». FORMAS: `Materia Melding` -> «Engarzar materia», `Meld` -> «Engarzar», `Extract Materia` -> «Extraer materia» (ya entregado en HowTo#97), `Retrieve Materia` -> «Recuperar materia».

The corpus was a genuine 9-9 tie, both halves in ordinary prose — «dentro de tu Data Center actual» against «fuera de tu centro de datos de origen» — and nothing inside the corpus could break it. What broke it was extracting the interface: once «DATA CENTER» exists as a menu row we must render, the word is no longer a translator's choice, it is something the player reads in two places at once. THE FAMILY IS NOW COHERENT AND MIRRORS THE ENGLISH CROWDING FAITHFULLY: blip -> «pip», bleep -> «blip», beep -> «bip», bloop -> «blup», bleeeeeep -> «bliiiiip», whirr -> «zumbido». #35807's English forces three distinct syllables in one line and «pip / blup / blip» delivers them.
